text: Vietnamese businesses among world's most optimistic about trade prospects: HSBC

Vietnamese businesses are among the most optimistic globally about international trade prospects, with 94% surveyed businesses expecting trade activities to grow over the next two years, according to HSBC's Global Trade Survey 2026 released on November 16.
Vietnam and the Philippines ranked highest in the survey on this indicator, compared with the global average of 86%.
The survey also highlighted cost pressures facing Vietnamese businesses.
Tariffs were the most frequently cited cost concern, mentioned by 52% of respondents in Vietnam, compared with 43% globally.
Energy costs ranked second, at 49%, against the global average of 44%.
Despite these pressures, Vietnamese businesses reported positive outcomes from supply chain adjustments.
Nine in ten respondents (90%) said these changes had improved their cash flow and working capital, significantly higher than the global average of 78%.
Almost all surveyed Vietnamese businesses (97%) said their measures to address trade uncertainty and disruptions had been effective, compared with 86% globally.
The survey also underscored the importance of trade agreements and regional networks.
Nearly all Vietnamese respondents (99.6%) said they were using at least one free trade agreement (FTA), compared with 95% globally.
However, 97% reported facing barriers that prevented them from making greater use of FTAs, exceeding the global average of 92%.
